concept.name: Selling climax
concept.definition: In Wyckoff's accumulation schematic, the selling climax (SC) is the terminal event of a decline: widening spread and climactic selling pressure as panicked public selling is absorbed by large interests near the lows, typically on the heaviest volume of the down-move. It is confirmed only after the automatic rally and a successful secondary test.
concept.intuition: Capitulation day: when the last fearful sellers dump their positions, stronger hands can finally buy in size without moving the price against themselves.
concept.mechanics: Marked by a wide-spread down bar on extreme volume after a mature decline; the SC low and the high of the ensuing automatic rally define the initial boundaries of the trading range around which the rest of the schematic (secondary test, spring, sign of strength) develops.
concept.failure_modes: In cascading markets driven by margin spirals or news shocks, apparent climaxes are followed by lower lows; the SC label is provisional until later tests hold.
concept.misconceptions: The selling climax is not 'the bottom'; it only ends the steepest phase of the decline, and accumulation typically takes weeks or months of range trading afterward.
concept.example: After a three-week slide, an index future sells off 3% intraday on quadruple average volume, then reverses to close flat; subsequent retests hold above the low on shrinking volume, and the flush is labeled the selling climax.
